name: Andrew Fastow

summary.text: Andrew S. Fastow was Enron's chief financial officer. The SEC charged him with fraud in October 2002 and a federal grand jury indicted him for fraud, money laundering and conspiracy the same month. On January 14, 2004 he pleaded guilty to two counts of conspiracy to commit securities and wire fraud, admitting he conspired with senior management to cause Enron to enter improper transactions with the LJM entities he controlled; he agreed to cooperate, to a 10-year sentence and to forfeit more than $29 million, and settled the SEC's civil case by disgorging more than $23 million. On September 26, 2006 he was sentenced to six years in prison.

facts.claim: The SEC charged Fastow with fraud on October 2, 2002, alleging among other things that the Raptor I entity owned by his LJM2 partnership was used to manipulate Enron's balance sheet and income statement and to generate profits for LJM2 and Fastow at Enron's expense; a federal grand jury indicted him on October 31, 2002 for fraud, money laundering and conspiracy.

facts.claim: Fastow and others at Enron formed the special purpose entity Chewco in 1997 to buy CalPERS' stake in the JEDI partnership and keep JEDI off Enron's balance sheet; the Enron board waived its conflict-of-interest rules to allow Fastow partial ownership and managerial roles in Chewco and LJM while on Enron's payroll.
